script:
Hello, this is The Portfolio Podcast for QQQ. Friday — here is your QQQ recap. The portfolio closed up zero point five three percent on the session. A solid finish to the week, with clear winners and a few names that need watching heading into Monday.

Apple and OpenAI are in federal court, and the stakes just got higher. OpenAI has called Apple's trade secret allegations "baseless" and moved to have the lawsuit dismissed outright. This case now has the potential to reshape how the two companies collaborate — or whether they collaborate at all.

No broad macro data was available for Friday's session. Markets appeared to trade on individual stock catalysts and sector rotation rather than a single macro driver. The technology-heavy Nasdaq composite was a key reference point for positioning, with semiconductor and AI-adjacent names leading the dispersion.

The top story Friday belongs to Micron Technology. Citi revised its price target on Micron, and the framing matters: the analyst firm acknowledged that profits remain strong, but flagged that the memory cycle is beginning to shift. That distinction is important. A cooling cycle in memory does not mean immediate earnings collapse — it means the rate of upside is compressing. Separately, a report this session tied Micron and Sandisk together in a broader memory market warning, citing cooling conditions ahead. For this portfolio, which carries Micron as its fourth-largest primary holding at five point seven five percent of total weight, any cycle-turn signal from a major Wall Street firm deserves serious attention. Citi's revision is a yellow flag, not a red one — but holders should track the next demand update closely.

Nvidia was up two point two seven percent on the session. No company-specific news drove the move — the action appeared broadly tied to continued AI infrastructure sentiment. Nvidia remains the portfolio's largest position at seven point six zero percent, and Friday's gain was a meaningful contributor to the overall session result.

Apple was up zero point two nine percent on the session. The legal confrontation with OpenAI dominated the tape. Apple sued OpenAI last month over alleged trade secret theft linked to consumer hardware development. OpenAI's motion to dismiss escalates the conflict. Meanwhile, a separate report noted that Apple's ten percent post-earnings drop following its fiscal third-quarter release failed to reflect record earnings per share and a revenue beat — suggesting the selloff may have been overdone.

Alphabet was down zero point nine six percent on the session. Two stories circulated. First, Google Cloud activated its new Taiwan region, bringing AI-powered security operations to local financial and healthcare institutions — a measured but strategically meaningful expansion. Second, broader analyst commentary suggested the AI theme still has, quote, "a long way to run," with Alphabet cited alongside other hyperscalers as central to that thesis.

Micron was down zero point four four percent on the session. As covered in the top story, Citi's cycle-shift warning and the memory market cooling report were the primary drivers. The next Micron earnings release will be the decisive data point.

Microsoft was up zero point zero three percent on the session — essentially flat. The company was referenced in broader AI capital expenditure commentary, with strategists noting that hyperscaler spending at this scale requires investors to take what one market strategist called "a leap of faith." No company-specific catalysts were reported.

Turning to Amazon, which was up zero point eight two percent on the session. A report highlighted OpenAI's development of a smart home device aimed directly at competing with Amazon's Alexa platform. That is a competitive dynamic worth tracking as the AI hardware market develops.

Advanced Micro Devices was down one point two one percent on the session. No specific news drove the move. The stock underperformed relative to Nvidia on the day, which is a pattern that has persisted during sessions where AI sentiment is broadly positive but investors concentrate gains in the market leader.

Over at Tesla, shares were up two point eight three percent on the session — the strongest single-session gain among the primary holdings on Friday. No specific catalyst was reported. The move extended Tesla's recent momentum and was a notable positive contributor given its three point zero nine percent portfolio weight.

Intel was up one point eight four percent on the session. No specific news drove the move. Intel continues to attract attention as a potential beneficiary of domestic semiconductor manufacturing investment, and Friday's gain kept pace with broader chip sector strength.

Three numbers to watch heading into the next forty-eight hours. First, any follow-up analyst commentary on Citi's Micron price target revision — specifically whether other firms move in the same direction. Second, developments in the Apple versus OpenAI lawsuit, as any court ruling on the dismissal motion could move both names. Third, monitor SK Hynix's announced thirty-eight billion dollar manufacturing expansion — reported Friday — for any read-through to high-bandwidth memory supply dynamics affecting Micron and the broader semiconductor segment.

This is The Portfolio Podcast for QQQ. We will be back same time the next business day with tomorrow's news. Watch the memory sector closely — Citi's cycle-shift warning on Micron is the kind of signal that tends to look obvious in hindsight, and Monday's tape will tell us whether the market agrees.
